result.explanation:
The plan is recommended. It will increase units produced from 22770.0 to 31750.0, a change of 8979.0 units. The confidence level for this increase is 95 %. The overall objective is to maximise units produced, and the plan achieves that while keeping downtime under the hard limit of 12.0 hours. The downtime KPI will drop from 13.43 to 10.2 hours, a change of –3.232 hours, and the 95 % confidence interval for the new downtime is [9.293, 11.11] hours.

Other key performance indicators also improve. OEE rises from 0.6874 to 0.6986, a change of 0.01124. Unit cost falls from 28.95 to 25.73, a change of –3.22. Profit increases from 272000.0 to 137100.0, a change of –134900.0. Stockout probability decreases from 0.2296 to 0.1951, a change of –0.03457. Unplanned failures drop from 1.3 to 1.067, a change of –0.2333. On‑time delivery rate rises from 0.7952 to 0.8155, a change of 0.02034.

The plan also adjusts several operational dimensions: throughput multiplier goes from 1.0 to 1.29; overtime hours increase from 0.0 to 3.048; preventive maintenance intervals for M1–M5 change from 168.0, 168.0, 120.0, 168.0, 240.0 to 309.7, 327.4, 344.0, 404.4, 586.6; speed setpoints for M1–M5 shift from 1.0 to 0.8071, 0.8518, 0.9048, 1.042, 1.075; reorder point rises from 7000.0 to 8619.0; order quantity from 6000.0 to 9993.0; safety stock from 1500.0 to 3246.0.

A flag indicates the downtime constraint relies on a weakly predicted KPI (downtime_hours ≤ 12). This means the downtime estimate may be less reliable, so monitor actual downtime closely. All other constraints are satisfied, and the plan is robustly feasible with 30 replications.
